data.name: Tiberius
data.gender_notes: Tiberius is used as a male name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: From the Latin word 'Tiberius', derived from the name of the Roman god Tiber, meaning 'River God'. In Christian tradition, it is the name of the Roman emperor who ruled during the time of Jesus' ministry. The name Tiberius carries the meaning “River God” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Hebrew, Greek. Parents who choose Tiberius usually hope their child will grow to embody river god and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes the power and strength of God's love and guidance in one's life.
data.etymology: Tiberius belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “River God.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Tiberius total 4, giving a life-path number of 4. Number 4 is linked with Rahu and with the qualities of stability, discipline and hard work.

in_hebrew.name: טיבריוס
in_hebrew.meaning: המשמעות של טיבריוס היא נהר טוב
in_hebrew.long_meaning: טיבריוס הוא שם שמקורו בלטינית ומשמעותו 'של נהר טיבר', נהר חשוב ברומא העתיקה. שם זה נמצא בשימוש גם בתקופה הנוצרית והפך לשם פרטי. במסורת הנוצרית, השם טיבריוס לא מוזכר ישירות בכתבי הקודש, אך הוא מוכר בשל קשרו לתקופת שלטונו של טיבריוס קיסר, שהיה קיסר רומא בתקופת ישו וראשית הנצרות.

in_greek.name: Τιβέριος
in_greek.long_meaning: Ο Τιβέριος είναι όνομα που προέρχεται από το λατινικό Tiberius, το οποίο σχετίζεται με τον ποταμό Τίβερις (Tiberis), ένα σημαντικό ποτάμι στην αρχαία Ρώμη. Στην Καινή Διαθήκη δεν υπάρχει άμεση αναφορά στο όνομα Τιβέριος, αλλά είναι γνωστό από την ιστορία ως το όνομα του Ρωμαϊκού Αυτοκράτορα Τιβέριος, που κυβέρνησε κατά την εποχή του Ιησού και την πρώιμη χριστιανική περίοδο.

in_latin.name: Tiberius
in_latin.meaning: Tiberius means of the Tiber river
in_latin.long_meaning: Tiberius is derived from the Latin name Tiberius, which is associated with the Tiber River, a significant waterway in ancient Rome. In Christian tradition, Tiberius is known as the name of a Roman Emperor, Tiberius Caesar, who ruled during the time of Jesus Christ and the early Christian church. The name Tiberius itself does not appear in the Bible but is historically significant in the context of early Christianity.

in_english.name: Tiberius
in_english.meaning: Of the Tiber river, associated with goodness
in_english.long_meaning: The name Tiberius originates from Latin, specifically from the name of the Tiber River in ancient Rome. It does not have a direct biblical reference but is historically significant as the name of the Roman Emperor Tiberius, who ruled during the lifetime of Jesus Christ. The name Tiberius conveys a sense of power, authority, and connection to one of the most important rivers in Roman history. In Christian tradition, while not directly mentioned in the Scriptures, Tiberius represents a figure from the early Christian era.

data.cultural_impact: The name "Tiberius" holds significant cultural importance due to the historical figure and Roman emperor who bore the same name. Tiberius (42 BC–37 AD) was the successor to Augustus Caesar and ruled from AD 14 to 37. The name represents the power and authority associated with Roman imperial rule.
data.spiritual_significance: From a spiritual standpoint, the name "Tiberius" carries a reminder of the political and societal climate during the time of Jesus' earthly ministry. With Tiberius as the ruler, religious and political tensions were high. The name serves as a stark reminder of the challenges and complexities facing early Christians, ultimately emphasizing the strength and resilience required to maintain their faith amidst the pressures and tribulations of the time.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Tiberius in the Bible represents the heavy burden of worldly power and authority. It is a reminder of the potential for darkness within even the most exalted positions, urging us to seek humility and serve others selflessly.

biblical_reference.note: The name Tiberius is not found in the Bible but is associated with Tiberius Caesar, mentioned in the New Testament (Luke 3:1).

modern_usage.modern_context: In today's world, the name Tiberius continues to be cherished by Christian families globally. It is frequently featured on social media platforms where parents share their naming journeys, and Christian name websites where expectant parents research meaningful Biblical names. The name bridges traditional Christian values with modern faith identity, making it relevant for contemporary families seeking names with deep spiritual and Biblical significance.
